newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN CHINA STEEL SHARE SALE FALLS SHORT OF MARK.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN CHINA STEEL SHARE SALE FALLS SHORT OF MARK.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday completed a four-day auction of shares in steel company China Steel which left 69 million of the 182 million shares in the offering unsold.
The auction saw the government sell 113.25 million of the steel giant's shares worth T$3.53 billion, leaving 68.94 million shares unsold, a stock exchange spokesman said.
The 182.19 million share sell-off, which was intended to reduce the state's stake in China Steel to 39.2 percent from 42.1 percent, will have to be resumed later, a stock exchange spokesman said.
"The Commission of National Corporations will have to sell the remaining shares at some other time," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone.
Thursday's shares were sold at an average price of T$31.11, almost the same as its T$31.10 closing price per share in the market in the day, the official said.
The sell-off was part of a five-year process to sell the state's entire China Steel stake, officials have said. China Steel, Taiwan's largest steel firm, was privatised in April 1995.
Taiwan's finance ministry last week auctioned some 418 million shares in Chiao Tung Bank -- a sell-off that reduced state's stake in the bank to 60.03 percent from 88.83 percent.
The government said in January it planned to release some 800 million state-owned shares worth some T$100 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (July/June).
The privatisation scheme is due to accelerate from the middle of 1998, with the government in July outlining plans to release state-owned shares worth T$450 billion over the next three fiscal years.
